# W.TestStrip: design for LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0 (LibKa0s v1.75.0, closes LibKa0s#48)

Read-only survey, done 2026-10-22, at these heads: LibKa0s `d9f9454` (master, unreleased v1.75.0, kit 40), DropWatcher `5611fe4`, LootHistory `8c79b23`, BankLedger `b0f9493`, MultiMeters `9638180`. The prior analysis (cluster `c48`) recommended *defer*. The owner has overruled that, so this document designs the promotion. It also shows how the design answers the analysis's objections under bars 2 and 3 (section 9).

---

## 1. What exists today (the source and the three markers it replaces)

| Addon | How test mode is marked today | Where | Body placement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **DropWatcher** (the source) | Strip `f.banner` between the filter bar and the panes. 18 px tall (`K.BANNER_H - 4`), 2 px under `f.filterHost`, amber fill `C.TONE.warn {1,0.65,0.15}` at 0.12 alpha, a 12x12 `NS.Icon("info")` at LEFT+6, a `GameFontNormalSmall` line at icon RIGHT+6, and the tooltip `NS.WindowTitleBar.TestTip` attached through `Window.AttachTooltip`. A title-bar word `TEST MODE` (`f.testText`) also shows | `modules/Window.lua:433-452` (buildBanner), shown at `:626`. Compact variant: `modules/CompactChrome.lua:365-377` (layoutStrip: shorter text, `SetWordWrap(compact)`, RIGHT anchor in compact only), `:452-456` (Paint: `SetHeight(BannerH()-4)`), `:473-482` (BannerH: one line, or `+ CC.WRAP_H` (12) when the unbounded width exceeds the room) | Panes re-anchored on every Refresh: `top = TAB_H + 4 + FILTER_H + (testMode and CC.BannerH() or 0)` (`Window.lua:479-486`) |
| **LootHistory** | A red `GameFontNormalLarge` `"TEST MODE"` on the title bar, hard-coded (not run through `L`), `SetTextColor(1,0.15,0.15)` | `modules/Browser.lua:887-892`. Toggled by `B:UpdateTestBadge()` (`:581-584`), which is called from `:575` (dataset swap) and `:1112` (Show) | Panes anchored **once**, at creation: `CreatePane` `top = titleBarH + tabStripH + contentGap + FILTERBAR_H(46) + FILTER_GAP(8)` (`:135-140`). `filterHost` at `:916-920` |
| **BankLedger** | The same badge, byte for byte | `modules/Browser.lua:992-997`; `B:UpdateTestBadge()` `:740-743`, called from `:1111` and `modules/Browser_Views.lua:301` | Panes anchored once at `paneTop = barTop + 46 + 8` (`:1012-1023`); `filterHost` `:1027-1031` |
| **MultiMeters** | A red `\|cffff2020TEST MODE\|r` appended to the title, plus `Test` on the session line. Both are header content: `frame.title:SetShown(header.show ~= false)` hides the marker when the player hides the header. This is the **header-hidden gap** | `modules/Window_Header.lua:339-343`, `:1193`; re-applied on `MSG.TEST_MODE_CHANGED` (`Window_Lifecycle.lua:95-103`) | No filter bar. The layout is built **from config only** (`Window.lua:338-378` BuildLayout, a secret-values rule: no widget geometry is read). `body` top = `pad + titleHeight + headerHeight` (`:714`), `headerFrame` top = `pad + titleHeight` (`Window_Header.lua:672`), `titleHeight = 0` when the header is hidden |

Nothing in any of the four suites pins LootHistory's or BankLedger's `testBadge`. MultiMeters pins its title marker (`tests/test_window_header.lua:593-608`). DropWatcher pins `f.banner` and `f.banner.text` across five suites (listed in section 6.1).

---

## 2. The contract

### 2.1 Placement and minor

- **Where it lives:** `LibKa0s/Widgets.lua`, the shell. It is about 45 lines and needs no new file. A new file would move the key's shape, need a `tests/majors.lua` entry and a `LibKa0s.xml` line, and touch the attach-file pairing. Widgets.lua is 655 lines now. With SearchBox (about 110) and TestStrip it reaches about 820, well under the 1500 cap and below the 1000 band.
- **Minor: one bump carries both new members.** `Widgets.lua` MINOR is **12** today (`Widgets.lua:36`) and the major key is `12.1.4.3.2`. W.SearchBox and W.TestStrip both land in the unreleased v1.75.0, so **both go out as Widgets minor 13 (key `13.1.4.3.2`)**. A file minor counts *released* changes (`docs/releasing.md` row 1: "every released change to that file"), and there is precedent for two changes sharing one bump: the 12.1.4.3.2 doc records that "the chart's half was briefly keyed 12.1.4.3.1 on the release branch; no release carried that key". Whichever item lands first bumps 12 to 13 and creates `docs/api/Widgets/version-13.1.4.3.2-docs.md` and `members-13.1.4.3.2.json`. The second adds its section and regenerates the manifest under the same key. The attach files (Reorder 1, DragHandle 4, LineChart 3, Autocomplete 2) re-pair on the shell's new minor through their `__*ShellMinor` probes, so none of their minors moves.
  - If the execution plan wants one minor per item instead (13 = SearchBox, 14 = TestStrip, key `14.1.4.3.2`), that also works. The cost is an API document for a key that never shipped. Not recommended.
- **Kit:** no change. The library does no measuring (2.4), so the mock needs no `GetUnboundedStringWidth`. Kit 41 (#46/#47) is independent.

### 2.2 Signature

```lua
--- The test-mode strip: a full-width band a window lays between its chrome and its data, saying the
--- data under it is not real. Draws itself and nothing else.
--- @param parent table          the frame to parent it to
--- @param opts table|nil        { text = string|nil, icon = string|number|nil }
---   text  the host's LOCALIZED line, set once at birth (nil -> ""); later changes go through strip.text
---   icon  a RESOLVED texture path or fileID (the host's NS.Icon("info")); nil -> no mark, text at LEFT+6
--- @return Frame strip  born HIDDEN, unanchored, HEIGHT tall, with:
---   strip.fill  Texture     BACKGROUND, all points, the collection's amber at 12%
---   strip.icon  Texture|nil ARTWORK, 12x12 at LEFT+6 (nil when opts.icon is nil)
---   strip.text  FontString  OVERLAY, GameFontNormalSmall, LEFT at icon RIGHT+6 (or strip LEFT+6),
---                           RIGHT at strip RIGHT-6, JustifyH LEFT, word wrap OFF (truncates with "...")
function lib.TestStrip(parent, opts)

--- Read-only layout numbers, published so a host lays out around the widget's own figures rather
--- than copying them (the DRAG_HANDLE / ROW_BOX precedent).
lib.TEST_STRIP = { HEIGHT = 18, RESERVE = 22 }   -- RESERVE = 2 gap + HEIGHT + 2 gap
```

Two members are added: `TestStrip` (function) and `TEST_STRIP` (table). The strip has **no methods**. This follows SearchBox's "no setters, the host writes `box.hint` directly" rule: the published fields are the surface.

### 2.3 What the strip does and does not do

**Does, at birth only:**
- Creates the Frame, its fill, its optional icon and its text.
- Calls `SetHeight(18)` once. It sets the colour, anchors its *own* regions, sets the initial text, and ends on `Hide()`. The DragHandle precedent applies: a widget born without an anchor must not flash at its parent's centre.

**Never, after the constructor returns:**
- Anchors itself, shows or hides itself, re-measures, or changes its own height or its text's anchors.

That is why a host's later `strip:SetHeight(h)`, `strip.text:SetText(...)` and `strip.text:SetWordWrap(true)` stick. DropWatcher's compact variant relies on exactly this (section 3).

**Deliberately not in it (recorded in the header's "WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT" block):**

| Omitted | Why |
|---|---|
| **A tooltip option** | Three hosts, three tooltip renderers. DropWatcher uses `Window.AttachTooltip` with TipMarks rows and keeps `widget.tooltip` for its suites. LootHistory and BankLedger use plain GameTooltip lines. MultiMeters wants none, so its body stays mouse-transparent. A library tooltip would either ignore DropWatcher's or grow a renderer. The strip is born with the mouse **off** (a bare `Frame`). A host that wants a tooltip enables the mouse and `HookScript`s OnEnter/OnLeave, which DropWatcher's `AttachTooltip` already does. |
| **A colour option** | All four adopters take the same look; that sameness is the point of promoting it ("two skins to keep in step", the file header). LibKa0s has no tone table. The amber is a file-local `STRIP_FILL = {1.00, 0.65, 0.15, 0.12}`, with a comment that it is DropWatcher's `C.TONE.warn` (`core/Constants.lua:149`) at 12%. Text colour comes from `GameFontNormalSmall` (gold), as in DropWatcher. A colour option can be added in a later minor if a consumer ever needs one. Adding it now would be an escape hatch that no consumer uses. |
| **Wrap, measure or a `:Height()` method** | Only DropWatcher's compact layout wraps, and MultiMeters *must not* measure (it lays out from config only). The two-line variant stays host-side, built on the published fields (section 3). |
| **Test-mode state** | The strip never reads test mode. The host decides when it shows and what it says. The name follows the owner's choice. |
| **Placement or body shift** | This is host layout. Hosts reserve `TEST_STRIP.RESERVE` while the strip is shown. |
| **An icon fallback** | `opts.icon = nil` is a valid, tested state: no mark, text at LEFT+6. Kit-40 caveat: a *pruned* icon still resolves to a path and draws blank, so **each adopter must declare `info`** on its `LibKa0s icons:` line (section 5). |

### 2.4 Height handling

- The one-line strip is **18 px** (`TEST_STRIP.HEIGHT`, DropWatcher's `K.BANNER_H - 4`).
- Hosts anchor it **2 px** below the chrome above it and push their body down by **`TEST_STRIP.RESERVE` = 22** (DropWatcher's `K.BANNER_H`) while it is shown, and by 0 while it is hidden.
- These numbers are constants, so MultiMeters can fold them into its config-only `BuildLayout`.
- A host with a two-line variant (DropWatcher's compact layout) sets the strip's height itself and adds its own extra to the reserve. The library publishes no wrap height: `CC.WRAP_H = 12` stays DropWatcher's own.

### 2.5 Localisation

The host passes localized text (`opts.text`, later `strip.text:SetText`). The library holds no strings. Each adopter adds its keys to `locales/enUS.lua`. LootHistory's and BankLedger's existing hard-coded `"TEST MODE"` badge text goes through `L` in the same change, which is a preview-mode rule item for v2.86.0.

### 2.6 Reference implementation (for the item's author)

```lua
-- Widgets.lua, after lib.CopyWindow
local STRIP_FILL = { r = 1.00, g = 0.65, b = 0.15, a = 0.12 }   -- DropWatcher's C.TONE.warn at 12%
local STRIP_H, STRIP_ICON, STRIP_INSET = 18, 12, 6
lib.TEST_STRIP = { HEIGHT = STRIP_H, RESERVE = STRIP_H + 4 }

function lib.TestStrip(parent, opts)
  opts = type(opts) == "table" and opts or {}
  local s = CreateFrame("Frame", nil, parent)
  s:SetHeight(STRIP_H)                       -- the local, not lib.TEST_STRIP: a host write cannot move it
  s.fill = s:CreateTexture(nil, "BACKGROUND")
  s.fill:SetAllPoints(s)
  s.fill:SetColorTexture(STRIP_FILL.r, STRIP_FILL.g, STRIP_FILL.b, STRIP_FILL.a)
  local icon = opts.icon
  if type(icon) == "string" or type(icon) == "number" then
    s.icon = s:CreateTexture(nil, "ARTWORK")
    s.icon:SetSize(STRIP_ICON, STRIP_ICON)
    s.icon:SetPoint("LEFT", s, "LEFT", STRIP_INSET, 0)
    s.icon:SetTexture(icon)
  end
  s.text = s:CreateFontString(nil, "OVERLAY", "GameFontNormalSmall")   -- from a template: never fontless
  if s.icon then s.text:SetPoint("LEFT", s.icon, "RIGHT", STRIP_INSET, 0)
  else s.text:SetPoint("LEFT", s, "LEFT", STRIP_INSET, 0) end
  s.text:SetPoint("RIGHT", s, "RIGHT", -STRIP_INSET, 0)
  s.text:SetJustifyH("LEFT")
  s.text:SetWordWrap(false)
  s.text:SetText(type(opts.text) == "string" and opts.text or "")
  s:Hide()
  return s
end
```

The RIGHT anchor is the one visible difference from DropWatcher's full layout today, which anchors LEFT only and lets text overflow. With both anchors and wrap off, the client truncates with an ellipsis. That is required for narrow meter windows. In DropWatcher's full layout the text fits, so it looks the same. In compact, DropWatcher already set this RIGHT anchor.

---

## 3. The compact variant: host-side, not an option

DropWatcher keeps its compact behaviour and builds it on the strip's published fields:

- `layoutStrip(f, compact)` (`CompactChrome.lua:365-377`) **drops its re-anchoring**, because the library already anchors LEFT and RIGHT. It keeps:
  - `b.text:SetText(compact and L[short] or L[full])`
  - `b.text:SetWordWrap(compact)`
- `CC.Paint`'s `f.banner:SetHeight(CC.BannerH() - 4)` and `CC.BannerH()`'s measurement stay as they are. `BannerH` reads `f.banner.text` and `GetWidth()`, which works the same now that the text always has both anchors (its `room` fallback still covers a zero width).
- `CC.WRAP_H` stays DropWatcher's own.

So the library carries no flag and no per-consumer branch (bar 2). The variant is presentation in one host, using the same contract every host uses.

---

## 4. MultiMeters: where the strip goes in a meter window

**Decision: at the top of the window, directly under the title strip and above the column-header row, always**, whether or not the header is shown.

```
pad
[ title strip ]            titleHeight   (0 when header.show == false)
  2px
[ TEST strip ]             18            (only while test mode is on; RESERVE 22 in all)
[ column headers ]         headerHeight
[ rows ... ]
```

Why there:
- It sits where the other three adopters put theirs, between the chrome and the data, so the grid is never read without passing the label.
- It is *not* header content, so it closes the header-hidden gap that the v2.86.0 preview-mode marker rule targets ("stays visible in every layout the display offers, a hidden header included").
- Its height is a constant, so MultiMeters' config-only layout rule holds: `BuildLayout` reads `NS.State.testMode` and a file-level `W` resolution, and no widget geometry.

**Rejected placements:**
- **Bottom of the body:** `rows.growthDirection == "UP"` anchors rows from the bottom, and a bottom band reads as status, not as a warning over the data.
- **An overlay on the rows:** it hides data and needs geometry reads.
- **"Force the title visible in test mode":** it changes `titleHeight` (and with it every anchor) behind the player's header setting, and puts the marker back inside the header the player asked to hide.

**Changes (all in MultiMeters):**
1. `modules/Window.lua` resolves `local W = LibStub and LibStub("LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0", true)` at file scope. Export_Modal already does this; there is no WidgetsSetup seam to reuse, so follow the repo's own pattern.
2. `BuildLayout` (`Window.lua:345-378`):
   - add `stripHeight = (W and NS.State and NS.State.testMode) and W.TEST_STRIP.RESERVE or 0` to the layout;
   - subtract it in `rowCapacity` (`:326-336`);
   - add it to `layout.minHeight` (`:376`).
3. Frame construction, beside `self.notice` (`:615-621`): `self.testStrip = W and W.TestStrip(frame, { text = L["TEST MODE: placeholder numbers, not your fight."], icon = NS.Icon and NS.Icon("info") })`. No tooltip, so the mouse stays off.
4. `ApplyConfig` (`:711-716`):
   - re-anchor the strip at `TOPLEFT frame pad, -(pad + titleHeight + 2)` and `TOPRIGHT frame -pad, same`;
   - body top becomes `pad + titleHeight + stripHeight + headerHeight`;
   - `SetShown(stripHeight > 0 and not minimized)`.
   - In `Window_Header.lua:672`, `headerFrame` top becomes `pad + titleHeight + stripHeight`.
5. `ApplyMinimized` (`Window_Header.lua:795-800`): hide the strip with the body. While minimized there is no data to mislabel, and the title marker remains whenever the header is shown.
6. `Window_Lifecycle.lua:95-103`, the `TEST_MODE_CHANGED` handler: replace `self:ApplyTitle()` with `self:RefreshUpvalues(); self:ApplyConfig()`, keeping `RefreshVisibility()` and `MarkDirty()`. The layout changes shape on the toggle, and the layout is only rebuilt there. `RefreshUpvalues` bumps `layoutVersion`, so rows re-anchor. `ApplyConfig` already calls `ApplyHeader`, which covers `ApplyTitle`.
7. **Keep** the red title marker (`Window_Header.lua:339-343`) and the session-line `Test` (`:1193`). The title word plus the strip is DropWatcher's reference form, and the marker covers the minimized and no-Widgets cases. (Open question 3.)

**Tests (`tests/test_window.lua`, `tests/test_window_header.lua`):**
- Test mode on: the strip is shown and its text matches. `body`'s TOPLEFT y = `-(pad + titleHeight + 22 + headerHeight)`; `headerFrame`'s y = `-(pad + titleHeight + 22)`.
- Test mode off: the strip is hidden and the offsets drop the 22.
- **`header.show = false` plus test mode: the strip is shown at y = `-(pad + 2)`.** This is the regression case for the header-hidden gap.
- Minimized: the strip is hidden.
- `layout.minHeight` and `maxRows` change by the reserve.
- With W nil (degraded), the window builds, nothing is reserved and the title marker still shows.
- The existing title-marker case at `:593-608` stays green.

**Smoke checks:**
- MM-TS-1: `/mm test` with the header shown. The strip is under the title, the column headers sit under it, and no row overlaps.
- MM-TS-2: header hidden in settings, then `/mm test`. The strip is at the top of the window.
- MM-TS-3: a narrow window. The text truncates with `...` inside the frame.
- MM-TS-4: toggle test mode off. The strip goes, the rows move back up, and the row count returns.
- MM-TS-5: minimize while in test mode. The strip hides.

---

## 5. Icon declaration (kit 40)

`Widgets.lua` cannot call Media (`Widgets.lua:12-17`), so each host resolves `NS.Icon("info")` and passes the path. Under kit 40's subset rule, a pruned `info` still resolves to a path and **draws blank, and the vendor gate cannot catch it** (CHANGELOG v1.75.0, "Declare the icons LibKa0s draws for you"). None of the four adopters has a `LibKa0s icons:` line yet. Each one's v1.75.0 re-vendor commit therefore adds it, and the list **must include `info`** next to the names the addon draws itself and the library-drawn set it wires (`close, copy, clear` for a debug console). `info` is also the Options id list's help mark, so most adopters need it anyway. In the CHANGELOG's v1.75.0 "What a consumer owes" list, add: "`W.TestStrip` adopters: `info`".

---

## 6. Per-adopter migration

Every adopter's item depends on (a) the LibKa0s TestStrip item and (b) that addon's v1.75.0 re-vendor (libs, kit, icons line, prune), because each suite loads the vendored copy. All four also add the strip's localized keys to `locales/enUS.lua`.

### 6.1 DropWatcher (moves its own copy into the library)

**Changes:**
- `core/WidgetsSetup.lua`: add `function NS.MakeTestStrip(parent, text)`, defined outside any `if W`. It answers `nil` when Widgets is absent, otherwise `W.TestStrip(parent, { text = text, icon = NS.Icon and NS.Icon("info") })`.
- `modules/Window.lua` buildBanner (`:433-452`) shrinks to these steps:
  1. `local b = NS.MakeTestStrip(body, L[full])`
  2. `if not b then return end`
  3. anchor to `f.filterHost` at 0/-2 left and right (as now)
  4. `Window.AttachTooltip(b, NS.WindowTitleBar.TestTip)`
  5. `f.banner = b`

  Delete its own fill, art, text, SetHeight and Hide: about 12 lines.
- `CompactChrome.lua`:
  - `layoutStrip` drops `ClearAllPoints`, both `SetPoint`s and `SetJustifyH` (the library owns them), and keeps `SetText` and `SetWordWrap(compact)`.
  - Rename every `b.art` reference to `b.icon`.
  - Guard `f.banner` nil in `layoutStrip`, `CC.Paint` (`:452-456`) and `CC.BannerH` (returns 0 with no banner).
  - `Window.Refresh` `:626` becomes `if frame.banner then ... end`.
  - With no Widgets: no strip, no reserve, and the title word still marks test mode.
- `core/Constants.lua:62`: keep `BANNER_H = 22`, with its comment changed to say it equals `Widgets.TEST_STRIP.RESERVE`. `test_surface_parity.lua:55` names it, so it stays.
- Update `Window.lua:4`'s header comment and the `buildBanner` comment ("the library's strip, anchored and tipped here").

**Tests:** the existing cases stay as they are, because they read `f.banner`, `f.banner.text`, `TooltipOf(f.banner)`, `GetHeight` and `__boundWidth`:
- `test_window.lua:94-104`
- `test_test_mode.lua:638-642`
- `test_window_shell.lua:82,113`
- `test_compact_chrome.lua:274-302`

New cases:
- `f.banner` is the library's strip: `f.banner.icon` texture == `NS.Icon("info")`, and the fill colour is amber at 0.12. Assert against literals, not `C.TONE`; this proves the look did not move.
- `K.BANNER_H == W.TEST_STRIP.RESERVE` and `K.BANNER_H - 4 == W.TEST_STRIP.HEIGHT`.
- Full layout: `f.banner.text` has a RIGHT point. Compact layout: wrap is on.
- Degraded (no Widgets): the window builds, test mode on raises no error, `f.banner == nil`, `layoutPanes` reserves 0 and `f.testText` is shown.

**Smoke checks:**
- DW-TS-1: `/dw test`, full layout. The strip looks identical to before (amber band, info mark, gold text) and its tooltip is unchanged.
- DW-TS-2: compact layout at 380 px. The short text wraps to two lines and the panes move down. At 520 px it is one line.
- DW-TS-3: combat ends test mode, and the strip and its reserve go.

### 6.2 LootHistory (badge kept, strip added)

**Changes:**
- `core/WidgetsSetup.lua`: add `NS.MakeTestStrip`, the same shape as DropWatcher's. The Widgets parity case (`tests/test_surface_parity.lua:87-110`) derives its members from the seam file's `function NS.` lines, so it covers the new member automatically, provided the function is defined on both paths.
- `modules/Browser.lua`:
  - After `filterHost` (`:916-920`): `frame.testStrip = NS.MakeTestStrip(frame, L["TEST MODE: a sample loot history, not yours. Combat ends it."])`. If it is non-nil, anchor TOPLEFT/TOPRIGHT to `filterHost`'s BOTTOMLEFT/BOTTOMRIGHT at y -2, and hook a tooltip: `EnableMouse(true)` plus OnEnter/OnLeave with GameTooltip lines "Test mode", "Shows: sample loot, holdings and timeline", "Ended by: combat, /lh test, the launcher menu".
  - `CreatePane` (`:135-140`) stops being the only place panes get anchored. Factor out `local function anchorPane(pane)`, using `top = … + FILTERBAR_H + FILTER_GAP + (stripShown and W.TEST_STRIP.RESERVE or 0)`. Read RESERVE through a `NS.TestStripReserve()` seam answer, or 0 when degraded.
  - Rename `B:UpdateTestBadge` to `B:UpdateTestStrip` and update both callers, `:575` and `:1112`. It now:
    - shows or hides the badge, as now;
    - shows or hides `frame.testStrip`;
    - re-anchors every pane.
  - The badge text becomes `L["TEST MODE"]`.
- The 22 px reserve comes out of the panes. Check that `minH` still leaves the table usable; nothing measured suggests otherwise.

**Tests (`tests/test_browser.lua`):** nothing pins the badge today. Add:
- Test mode on: the strip is shown with its L text, the pane TOPLEFT y moves by -22, and the badge is shown.
- Test mode off: both are hidden and y is back at the base.
- Show while already in test mode (the `:1112` path) reserves the space.
- The strip is anchored to `filterHost` (`GetPoint`).
- Degraded (no Widgets): no strip, no shift, and the badge still shows.

**Smoke checks:**
- LH-TS-1: `/lh test`. The strip sits under the filter bar, the History table starts under it, and the badge is still on the title.
- LH-TS-2: the Insights and Timeline tabs are shifted the same way.
- LH-TS-3: entering combat removes the strip and the panes move back up.
- LH-TS-4: hovering the strip shows its tooltip.

### 6.3 BankLedger (the same as LootHistory)

BankLedger has **no WidgetsSetup seam**: `W` is resolved in `modules/Browser.lua` (and Export.lua).

**Changes:**
- In `Browser.lua` after `filterHost` (`:1027-1031`): `frame.testStrip = W and W.TestStrip(frame, { text = L["TEST MODE: a sample ledger, not your bank. Combat ends it."], icon = NS.Icon and NS.Icon("info") })`, with the same anchor and tooltip as LootHistory ("Ended by: combat, /bl test, the launcher menu").
- The pane loop (`:1017-1023`) becomes an `anchorPanes()` helper that uses the reserve.
- Rename `B:UpdateTestBadge` (`:740-743`) to `B:UpdateTestStrip` and update its callers, `:1111` and `Browser_Views.lua:301`. It does the same three things as LootHistory's.
- The badge text becomes `L["TEST MODE"]`.
- The Widgets parity: BankLedger's by-name list does not project Widgets, so it needs no edit.

**Tests and smoke:** the same as LootHistory, in `tests/test_browser.lua`. Smoke BL-TS-1 to BL-TS-4 mirror LH-TS-1 to LH-TS-4 (`/bl test`, the ledger tabs, combat end, tooltip).

### 6.4 Interaction with the new simulators (owner decision 2)

The LootHistory and BankLedger simulators on Sim-1.0 are a separate item. The strip holds no state, so if a later design wants a simulation band, the host can reuse the same strip with its own text. That is not in scope here: DropWatcher shows its strip for test mode only, and its simulation is marked by its title word and footer.

---

## 7. LibKa0s deliverables

1. **`LibKa0s/Widgets.lua`:**
   - `lib.TestStrip` and `lib.TEST_STRIP` (section 2.6), MINOR 13. This is shared with SearchBox: whichever lands second does not bump again.
   - The header's first line names the strip, and a short "WHY THIS IS A LIBRARY" paragraph cites #48 and the owner's 2026-10-22 ruling.
   - "WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT" gains the five omissions from section 2.3, each with its re-check trigger: "a consumer needs a different colour, a tooltip renderer or a measured height with the same semantics as another".
2. **`tests/test_widgets_teststrip.lua`** (new), registered in `tests/run.lua`'s suite list (`:81`, after `test_widgets_autocomplete`). It installs `tests/fixture_geom.lua` per case, as `test_widgets.lua` does. For `SetJustifyH`, `SetWordWrap` and `SetTexture` recording, stub them locally on the built regions; `fixture_geom` already records `SetColorTexture` and points. Cases:
   - born hidden, unanchored (`GetNumPoints() == 0`) and 18 tall, with `fill`, `icon` and `text` present;
   - the fill is `1, 0.65, 0.15, 0.12`, all points;
   - an icon path gives `icon` its texture, 12x12 at `LEFT,+6`, with the text's LEFT on the icon's RIGHT at +6;
   - `opts.icon = nil` gives `strip.icon == nil` and the text's LEFT at strip LEFT +6;
   - a numeric fileID is accepted;
   - the text is built from `GameFontNormalSmall`, with a RIGHT point at -6, JustifyH LEFT and wrap false;
   - `opts.text` is set, and nil, a non-table opts or a non-string text each give `""`;
   - the constructor never enables the mouse; a host can `EnableMouse` and `HookScript("OnEnter")`, and its hook runs;
   - a host `SetHeight(30)` and a host `text:SetWordWrap(true)` stick (nothing re-asserts them);
   - `TEST_STRIP.RESERVE == TEST_STRIP.HEIGHT + 4`;
   - writing `lib.TEST_STRIP.HEIGHT = 99` does not change the next strip's height (the local is authoritative);
   - two strips share no regions.
3. **`docs/api/Widgets/version-13.1.4.3.2-docs.md`** (new, Current). In "What changed at 13.1.4.3.2", a TestStrip section: signature, fields, birth-only contract, height and reserve, what it is not, the icon-declaration note. Member rows: `TestStrip` and `TEST_STRIP`, **Since 13**. Mark the 12.1.4.3.2 doc *Superseded by* and add its "Moving to 13.1.4.3.2" section. Generate **`members-13.1.4.3.2.json`** with `lua tools/gen-api-members.lua`; it adds `TestStrip` (function) and `TEST_STRIP` (table). Add the row to `docs/api/README.md`.
4. **`docs/api/CONSUMERS.md`:** rows for `lib.TestStrip` and `lib.TEST_STRIP` as a host duplicate (DropWatcher) until the four adopters land, then as consumers LootHistory, BankLedger, MultiMeters and DropWatcher.
5. **`CHANGELOG.md` v1.75.0:**
   - the version block becomes `Widgets` key **13.1.4.3.2** (the same edit SearchBox makes);
   - add a "`W.TestStrip`" section;
   - in "What a consumer owes", add "declare `info`" for adopters.
   - `test_versioning` enforces that the block and `MODULES` agree.
6. Close **LibKa0s#48** with a pointer to the commit, once the four adopters land.

---

## 8. Standard (v2.86.0) touch points

- **library-stack-§7 module table, the Widgets row:** add "from **Widgets minor 13 (`LibKa0s v1.75.0`)**, `SearchBox` and **`TestStrip`**: the test-mode strip a window lays between its chrome and its data, with **`Widgets.TEST_STRIP`** (`HEIGHT`, `RESERVE`). It draws itself only; the text, tooltip, placement, body shift and when it shows stay the host's, and the icon arrives as a resolved path, so an adopter declares `info`."
- **The preview-mode marker rule** (owner decision 3): it may name `Widgets.TestStrip` as the shared form for a window with a filter bar or a data grid. Per the analysis, the title word stays acceptable on its own for displays without one. The rule's "visible in every layout, a hidden header included" clause is what the MultiMeters placement satisfies.
- **The closed set of library-drawn icons** (§7): `TestStrip` draws only the icon the host passes, so it adds nothing to that set. Its adopters still owe `info` because they pass it. State that in the rule so the set stays closed.

---

## 9. How this answers the analysis's objections

| Objection (c48) | Answer in this design |
|---|---|
| Bar 1: one consumer | The owner names four. The design gives each the same semantics: a band between chrome and data, saying the data is not real, shown only in test mode, with the same look. |
| Bar 2: the compact wrap and measure would need flags | It has no flags. The compact variant is built host-side on the published fields (section 3), the library never measures, and the birth-only contract makes the host's changes stick. |
| Bar 3: the colour is addon-local and gets restyled | The look is fixed in the library (the file-local amber). A restyle becomes a library minor that every adopter takes together, which is exactly the "two skins" argument. |
| "The art must arrive resolved" | Yes: `opts.icon`, with the kit-40 declaration owed (section 5). |
| "Hosts keep anchoring and body shift anyway" | Yes. `TEST_STRIP.RESERVE` is published so they stop copying 22. |

---

## 10. Suggested item breakdown (for the execution plan)

| ID (suggested) | Repo | Depends on | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| LK-TS | LibKa0s: Widgets.lua strip, tests, API doc and manifest, CONSUMERS, CHANGELOG | LK-SB if SearchBox lands first (it bumps the minor), otherwise none | S |
| DW-TS | DropWatcher | LK-TS, DW re-vendor v1.75.0 (`info` declared) | S |
| LH-TS | LootHistory | LK-TS, LH re-vendor | S |
| BL-TS | BankLedger | LK-TS, BL re-vendor | S |
| MM-TS | MultiMeters | LK-TS, MM re-vendor | M (layout, lifecycle, tests) |
| STD-TS | WowAddonStandards library-stack-§7 row and preview-mode reference | LK-TS | S |

Each addon's green gate is `lua tests/run.lua` and `luacheck .` at 0/0, with every file under 1500 lines. Size after the change, against the cap:

| File | Lines now | Lines after (about) |
|---|---|---|
| LH Browser.lua | 1231 | 1260 |
| BL Browser.lua | 1179 | 1205 |
| MM Window.lua | 1352 | 1375 |
| MM Window_Header.lua | 1233 | (minor change) |

In-client smoke checks DW/LH/BL/MM-TS-n are the owner's to run and are recorded in the bundle's smoke-test file.

Widgets minor: one bump to 13 carrying both W.SearchBox and W.TestStrip (recommended, key 13.1.4.3.2), or one minor per item (13 then 14, key 14.1.4.3.2, which leaves an API document for a key that never shipped)?

MultiMeters: keep the red title marker and the session-line 'Test' word alongside the strip (recommended for the minimized and no-Widgets cases), or drop one or both now that the strip is always visible?

MultiMeters: is it acceptable that test mode costs about one row of capacity at the default window size (the 22 px reserve), and that the TEST_MODE_CHANGED handler now runs RefreshUpvalues + ApplyConfig instead of ApplyTitle?

Strip wording for each addon (proposed: LH 'TEST MODE: a sample loot history, not yours. Combat ends it.'; BL 'TEST MODE: a sample ledger, not your bank. Combat ends it.'; MM 'TEST MODE: placeholder numbers, not your fight.'). MultiMeters' ending condition was not verified, so its line does not claim one.

# Design: `LibKa0s-Glow-1.0`, the stateless LibCustomGlow-1.0 driver (LibKa0s v1.75.0, Glow minor 1)

Status: design for the v1.75.0 run. Read-only survey done 2026-10-22 against working trees at LibKa0s `d9f9454` (master, unreleased v1.75.0, kit 40), WowAddonStandards v2.85.0, and DropWatcher, QuickComms and KickCD as they are checked out today. The three hosts vendor a byte-identical `libs/LibCustomGlow-1.0/LibCustomGlow-1.0.lua` (md5 `78fd0531…`, `MINOR_VERSION = 24`, 955 lines). Every LCG line cited below is from that file.

## 1. Decisions in one place

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | New major `LibKa0s-Glow-1.0`, one file `LibKa0s/Glow.lua`, minor 1. Floor is `NEEDS_CORE = 1` only, and no Core member is called. | The owner has accepted it. This is the Env/Pool/Item pattern: it floors so that a partial payload leaves every module absent. |
| D2 | The surface is exactly two members, `Start(frame, style, knobs, key, frameLevel)` and `Stop(frame, style, key)`, besides `MAJOR`, `MINOR` and `MODULES`. | It is the smallest contract that serves all three hosts with the same semantics. The challenger's scope cut drops `G.Available()`. |
| D3 | `frameLevel` is a **fifth, optional positional argument**, not a knob. | It says where the host stacks the effect. It is not a player setting. DW and QC pass a constant 2, and KickCD passes nothing (LCG's 8 over its own +5 child). Putting it in `knobs` would make DW write a constant into the profile-derived `cfg` (Glow.lua `read`) and QC write one into the signature-bearing `g` (IconStyle.lua `glowConfig`). Bar 2 allows exactly one optional presentation argument. **Owner check:** the brief sketched 4 arguments (see open questions). |
| D4 | `color` lives **in `knobs`** (`knobs.color`, an `{r,g,b,a}` array). | The owner's 4-argument shape has no colour slot. DW `cfg.color` and QC `g.color` are already arrays in exactly that place, and KickCD sets one field on its reused table. |
| D5 | Style vocabulary is closed: `"button"`, `"proc"`, `"pixel"`, `"autocast"`. These are lowercase strings, exactly what all three hosts store. There are no aliases, and an unknown style is a quiet no-op (`false`). | LCG's own names are "Action Button Glow", "Proc Glow", "Pixel Glow" and "Autocast Shine". The owner's "Button/Action" is LCG's "Action Button Glow" and maps to `"button"`. Aliases would be an escape hatch. |
| D6 | **No `STYLES` member.** The four names are documented vocabulary, pinned by the library's tests. | No host could use a list. DW's `GLOW_STYLES` (SchemaRows.lua:152) is a localized `choices{}` table, QC's `D.GLOW_STYLES` drives its own dropdown in its own order, and KickCD's styles live in its settings rows. A member nobody reads is a member nobody tests, and it stays additive-only forever. |
| D7 | **Knob RANGES are not published (rejected).** See §5. | Ranges are slider policy, not LCG facts. Every host keeps its own table regardless (defaults, keys, kind vocabulary, labels, order). |
| D8 | **No defaults.** A `nil` knob reaches LCG as `nil`, so LCG's own value applies. Two traps are coerced, with nothing else: `pixelLength` (a number > 0, otherwise `nil`) and the two booleans (`false` only when `false`). A numeric knob that is not a number becomes `nil`. | This is the owner's "NO defaults". It is also the challenger's scope cut: the DW/QC `num(v, 0)` and `num(v, 1)` fallbacks are not baked in, because LCG's nil value is the same number. |
| D9 | LCG is resolved **at every call** with `LibStub("LibCustomGlow-1.0", true)`, with no memo. If LCG is absent, `Start` answers `false` and `Stop` does nothing. | Bus/AceEvent is the precedent (Bus.lua:31-32). The call is one LibStub index, negligible next to LCG's own work, and it is never per-frame. KickCD's worst path is a `Stop` per not-ready `SPELL_STATE`, which is event-driven. Call-time resolution is also what lets every host suite inject its fake LCG after load. A memo was rejected: it adds state to a stateless driver and a staleness argument (LibStub upgrades in place, so it would be safe, but it still has to be argued) to save nothing measurable. |
| D10 | Each LCG member is presence-checked (`type(fn) == "function"`) before it is called. | The library cannot floor on a consumer-vendored third-party lib (library-stack-§6/§7). A host whose LCG copy is older than ProcGlow (or is someone else's winning copy) gets `false`, not an error inside the library. |
| D11 | No lifecycle, signature, unchanged-repaint gate, proc-burst spend, trigger, class-colour resolution, stop-before-start, `GlowGroup` composer or catalog. | All rejected (#56). §7 below records them under "What is not here". |

## 2. The contract (what `docs/api/Glow/version-1-docs.md` publishes)

### `Glow.Start(frame, style, knobs, key, frameLevel) -> boolean`

- `frame`: the frame the effect is drawn around. If it is `nil`, the call returns `false` and nothing is called. LCG's `_Start` functions return on a nil frame, but its `_Stop` functions do not all do so (`ButtonGlow_Stop` and `ProcGlow_Stop` index `r` unguarded, LCG:750, :945), so the driver guards both members the same way.
- `style`: one of the four names. Anything else returns `false`.
- `knobs`: a table, or `nil`, which is read as an empty table (a shared constant, no allocation). Any other type is also read as empty. Fields the driver does not name are ignored, so a host can pass its whole config table (DW `cfg`, QC `g`).
- `key`: the caller's identity string, passed through unchanged. `nil` is LCG's shared empty key `""`, so the doc says *pass your addon's own key*. The `button` style takes no key.
- `frameLevel`: a number or `nil` (LCG uses 8). It is relative to `frame` (LCG `r:GetFrameLevel() + frameLevel`, LCG:133, :671, :717, :933).
- It returns `true` when it called LCG's `_Start` for that style. It returns `false` when the frame is nil, the style is unknown, LCG is absent, or the style's `_Start` is missing.
- It does **not** stop anything first. Switching styles is the host's job: stop the old one, then start the new one. All three hosts already do this.

### `Glow.Stop(frame, style, key)`

- `style` given: only that style's `_Stop`. `button` gives `ButtonGlow_Stop(frame)` with no key. The others give `X_Stop(frame, key)`.
- `style == nil`: **all four**, in KickCD's order (Button, Pixel, AutoCast, Proc). This is KickCD's shape (IconGrid_Render.lua:388-396). Per the brief the `style?` stays optional, overriding the challenger's suggestion to drop stop-all.
- An unknown style **string** is a no-op. Only `nil` means all four.
- A nil frame or an absent LCG is a no-op. A missing `_Stop` member is skipped. It returns nothing.

### Knob → LCG argument mapping (the contract table)

`num(v)` is `v` when `type(v) == "number"`, otherwise `nil`.

| Style | LCG call (LCG line) | Arguments, in order |
|---|---|---|
| `pixel` | `PixelGlow_Start(r,color,N,frequency,length,th,xOffset,yOffset,border,key,frameLevel)` (:260) | `frame, knobs.color, num(pixelLines), num(pixelFrequency), length(pixelLength), num(pixelThickness), num(xOffset), num(yOffset), pixelBorder ~= false, key, frameLevel` |
| `autocast` | `AutoCastGlow_Start(r,color,N,frequency,scale,xOffset,yOffset,key,frameLevel)` (:399) | `frame, knobs.color, num(autocastParticles), num(autocastFrequency), num(autocastScale), num(xOffset), num(yOffset), key, frameLevel` |
| `button` | `ButtonGlow_Start(r,color,frequency,frameLevel)` (:657) | `frame, knobs.color, num(buttonFrequency), frameLevel` (no key) |
| `proc` | `ProcGlow_Start(r, options)` (:915) | `frame, { color = knobs.color, startAnim = procStartAnim ~= false, duration = num(procDuration), xOffset = num(xOffset), yOffset = num(yOffset), key = key, frameLevel = frameLevel }`, a **fresh table per call** |

The knob names are the DW/QC camelCase spellings, and the published vocabulary is these fourteen fields: `color, pixelLines, pixelFrequency, pixelLength, pixelThickness, pixelBorder, autocastParticles, autocastFrequency, autocastScale, buttonFrequency, procDuration, procStartAnim, xOffset, yOffset`. KickCD's PascalCase leaves map to them by lower-casing the first letter (`XOffset` → `xOffset`, `ButtonFrequency` → `buttonFrequency`, and so on, all 13 exact).

### The traps, written into the doc

1. **`pixelLength` 0 means automatic.** LCG computes the length only for `nil` (`length = length or floor(...)`, LCG:283). A 0 would draw zero-length lines. The driver passes a number > 0 through and sends 0, negatives and non-numbers as `nil`.
2. **`pixelBorder` draws for anything but `false`.** LCG tests `if not(border==false)` (:303), so `nil` draws the dark border. The driver passes `pixelBorder ~= false`, a real boolean with LCG's own nil meaning: a host that wants no border passes `false`. The same rule applies to `procStartAnim`, where LCG's default is `true` (ProcGlowDefaults, :903-911).
3. **The proc options table must be fresh.** `ProcGlow_Start` calls `setmetatable(options, …)` on whatever it is handed (:920). The driver never hands over the caller's `knobs`, and it does not reuse a scratch table. DW's test reads `lib.calls[n][3].color` / `.duration` after later calls (test_glow.lua:166, :183-200), so a reused scratch would corrupt those recordings. LCG allocates a metatable per proc start anyway, so a fresh options table costs nothing extra. It is also what all three hosts do today.
4. **`color` is retained by reference** by the button style (`f.color = color`, LCG:704, :728). On a restart that reuses the frame, LCG divides the old alpha by `f.color[4]` (:700). A host **must not mutate** a colour array after handing it over. Hand over a fresh array, or one that never changes. DW builds `cfg.color` once per settings generation, QC builds `g.color` per config build, and KickCD allocates `{ r, gr, b, a }` per restart (IconGrid_Render.lua:503). All three comply, and the doc makes it a rule.
5. **The `button` style has no key.** Each frame has one Blizzard-style glow (`r._ButtonGlow`). Two keyed callers on one frame cannot both use `button`, and `Stop(frame, nil, key)` stops any button glow on the frame, whoever started it. **Use stop-all only on a frame you own.** KickCD's own glow child qualifies. QC already keeps its two glows on two frames (`qcIconFrame` under `QuickCommsIcon`, `qcEdge` under `QuickCommsButton`). This is the challenger's missed item, so the doc states it.
6. **`ButtonGlow_Stop` on a visible frame animates out** and releases later (:750-761). A restart inside that window reuses `r._ButtonGlow`. This is LCG behaviour, transparent to the driver, and recorded so nobody "fixes" it.
7. **Combat.** LCG's frames are plain children, so the driver makes no protected call. QC already relies on this for hover and send glows in combat (QC Glow.lua header).

## 3. `LibKa0s/Glow.lua` (implementation spec)

The file is about 110 lines including the header. The header explains why it exists (three hosts mapped the same knobs to the same positional arguments, with the same two traps) and what it deliberately is not (the §7 list). Shape:

```lua
local core = LibStub and LibStub("LibKa0s-Core-1.0", true)
local NEEDS_CORE = 1
if not core or (core.MINOR or 0) < NEEDS_CORE then return end   -- no NewLibrary; module absent

local MAJOR, MINOR = "LibKa0s-Glow-1.0", 1
local lib = LibStub:NewLibrary(MAJOR, MINOR)
if not lib then return end
lib.MAJOR, lib.MINOR = MAJOR, MINOR
lib.MODULES = lib.MODULES or {}
lib.MODULES.Glow = MINOR

local LCG = "LibCustomGlow-1.0"
local NONE = {}                                   -- nil knobs: read nothing, allocate nothing
local function lcg() return LibStub and LibStub(LCG, true) end   -- CALL time, every call
local function num(v) if type(v) == "number" then return v end end
local function len(v) if type(v) == "number" and v > 0 then return v end end
-- START[style](L, frame, k, key, level) -> boolean; each checks type(L.X_Start) == "function"
-- STOP[style](L, frame, key); ORDER = { "button", "pixel", "autocast", "proc" } for stop-all
function lib.Start(frame, style, knobs, key, frameLevel) ... end
function lib.Stop(frame, style, key) ... end
```

- Members are dot-called (`G.Start(...)`), like Pool and Item.
- The non-proc styles allocate nothing in the driver. KickCD's `startEffect` closure `k` (IconGrid_Render.lua:449) goes away, so KickCD's hot path ends slightly lighter, not heavier. This resolves the analyst's allocation risk.
- The file is not secret-sensitive. It reads no unit data.

### `tests/test_glow.lua` (headless, with a fake LCG)

The fake is registered on the instance's LibStub (as DW and QC's tests do: `m.LibStub:NewLibrary("LibCustomGlow-1.0", 24)`). Each `_Start` and `_Stop` records `{ name, n = select("#", ...), ... }`. Every case says what turns it red.

1. **Absent LCG:** `Start` → `false` for all four styles, `Stop` with and without a style does not raise, and nothing is recorded. *Red under:* a load-time capture or an unguarded `L.X`.
2. **Call-time resolution:** the Glow module loads with no LCG, the fake is registered afterwards, and `Start("pixel")` reaches it. *Red under:* `local L = LibStub(LCG, true)` at file load (KickCD's current shape).
3. **Pixel vector:** with every knob set, all 11 positions are asserted, including `key` at 10 and `frameLevel` at 11.
4. **`pixelLength`:** 0, -3, `"6"` and `nil` each give `nil`. 6 gives 6.
5. **Booleans:** `pixelBorder` false gives `false`. `true`, `nil` and `"x"` give `true`. The same holds for `procStartAnim` via the options table.
6. **Numeric type guard:** `pixelLines = "8"` gives `nil`, and so do `xOffset = "3"` and `procDuration = {}`.
7. **AutoCast vector** (9 positions) and **Button vector** (4 positions, with no key in position 4: `frameLevel` is there).
8. **Proc:** the options table is not `knobs` (`rawequal` false), `getmetatable(knobs) == nil` after the call, the table is new per call (two calls give two tables), and its fields are as in the mapping table. `nil` knobs give absent fields except `startAnim = true`.
9. **`knobs == nil`** and **`knobs = "x"`**: every positional slot is `nil` and the call still happens.
10. **Unknown style** (`"Pixel"`, `"action"`) and **nil frame**: `false`, and no call.
11. **Missing member:** a fake without `ProcGlow_Start` / `ProcGlow_Stop` gives `Start("proc")` → `false`, `Stop(f, "proc", k)` is a no-op, and `"pixel"` still works.
12. **Stop:** `Stop(f, "pixel", "K")` records exactly `PixelGlow_Stop(f, "K")`. `Stop(f, "button", "K")` records `ButtonGlow_Stop(f)` with `n == 1`. `Stop(f, nil, "K")` records all four in order. `Stop(f, "bogus", "K")` records nothing.
13. **Stateless:** `Start` never records a `_Stop`, and repeated `Start` calls record repeated `_Start` calls (no gate).
14. **Surface:** `test_versioning` already compares `members-1.json` against the live module. Add a lint-style assertion that `Glow.lua` names no `LibStub(...)` outside `lcg()` and the Core probe.

The generic suites (`test_versioning`, `test_loader`) cover the floor: Core absent or too low means the major is not registered, because they iterate `T.majors`.

Each adopter gets **`core/GlowSetup.lua`**, published as **`NS.GlowLib`**. `NS.Glow` is already DW and QC's host lifecycle module, and the same name is used in all three hosts:

```lua

-- same thing an absent LibCustomGlow-1.0 already means here. Never a local copy of the mapping.
local G = LibStub and LibStub("LibKa0s-Glow-1.0", true)

    Start = function() return false end,
    Stop  = function() end,

Each host's `tests/test_surface_parity.lua` gains `T.assertSurfaceParity(degraded.GlowLib, "LibKa0s-Glow-1.0")` with an empty ignore set.

Anywhere after the libs block and before …`).

## 5. Knob ranges: decision is **do not publish** (agrees with the challenger)

Reasons, strongest first:

1. **The ranges are UI policy, not LCG facts.** LCG accepts any `N > 0`, any frequency (a negative one runs backwards, :272-279), any thickness and any length (clamped to the frame by LCG itself, :284). `1..20` lines and `0.05..2` frequency are the owner's slider choices from KickCD's feedback-21 table. A published range is additive-only forever: widening one slider in one addon would either need a library release or fork the range.
2. **No host table is saved.** Every host still needs its own table for defaults (KickCD `PixelFrequency` 0.25 against DW/QC 0.1, an owner decision at DW defaults/Profile.lua:24-26), key spelling (PascalCase `leaf` against camelCase `key`), kind vocabulary (`number`/`bool` against `slider`/`bool`), labels, tips and order (DW offsets first per feedback-24, QC on DW's older order, KickCD button first). With all of that stripped, 13 rows of min/max/step are low-content data, and "MUST NOT promote on frequency alone" (library-stack §7 bars) keeps it inline.
3. **Clamping is host safety policy.** KickCD clamps every read (`knobValue`, IconGrid_Render.lua:417-430) because a hand-edited 900-line pixel glow freezes the client. That is a default and a policy, which the owner excluded. It stays in KickCD. DW and QC rely on their schema's write validation. A shared clamp would be a behaviour change for DW and QC.
4. **The drift risk is already covered.** Each host's own suite pins its ranges (KickCD test_icongrid_glow_knobs.lua; DW test_schema_rows.lua:222-224; QC's schema tests). A library range table adds a cross-repo join and protects nothing extra at runtime.

**Re-check trigger** (recorded in the API doc's "What is not here" and in the #56 closing comment): a fourth consumer copies the knob table, or one host edits a range and the others do not.

- **Delete:** `local LCG = LibStub(...)` (:347), `KNOB_INDEX` (:406, :410), `startEffect` (:448-470) and the four direct LCG stops (:393-396).
- **Change:**
  - Build `FIELD[i] = leaf:sub(1,1):lower() .. leaf:sub(2)` once, beside `KNOB_KEYS` (:405-411). `readKnobs` (:432-442) then writes `vals[FIELD[i]]` instead of `vals[i]`. The table is still the icon's own `self._glowKnobs`, made once, so there is no new allocation.
  - `StopGlow` (:388-396) becomes `local g = self.glow; if not g then return end; NS.GlowLib.Stop(g, nil, LCG_KEY); self._glowKind, self._glowColor = nil, nil`. Stop-all is safe because `g` is KickCD's own child frame (trap 5).
  - In `StartGlow` (:474-507), the `if not (g and LCG)` gate becomes `if not g then return end`. Then come the colour resolve, the knob read and the unchanged idempotency gate, then `self:StopGlow()`, `vals.color = c` (fresh `c` as today), and `if not NS.GlowLib.Start(g, kind, vals, LCG_KEY) then return end`, and finally `_glowKind` and `_glowColor` as today. There is no fifth argument: LCG keeps its 8. When the return is `false` (LCG absent), no state is recorded, which is today's outcome. The early-exit position moves, with no visible effect (divergence 13).
- **Stays:** the `LCG_KEY` and its long comment (re-pointed: "the driver's Stop/Start take the key"), `unpackGlowColor`, `knobValue` clamp, `Const.GLOW_KNOBS`, triggers, `applyInterruptibleMask`, the `+5` glow child, `IconGrid.lua:237`'s pool-release `StopGlow`, and the DebugLogSetup `OPTIONAL_LIBS` line.
- **New:** `core/GlowSetup.lua`, a TOC line after `core\PoolSetup.lua` (the same "before modules\IconGrid*" constraint), and a parity case.
- **Tests:**
  - `tests/test_icongrid_glow_knobs.lua` stays unchanged. Its positional assertions (:164-235) and proc-options assertions (:190-192) are exactly the driver's output. Its `T.load` hook injects the recording LCG into `mocks.__libs`, which the kit LibStub reads at call time.
  - `test_flow_traces.lua:322-330` (LCG absent) stays unchanged.
  - **Add one case:** "StopGlow stops all four styles under the KickCD key, the button style keyless". The current suite records `_Stop` calls as no-ops, so stop-all is not pinned today.

### Review check for all three

Run `grep -rn "Glow_Start\|Glow_Stop" --include='*.lua' . | grep -v '/libs/\|tests/'` in each host. It must return nothing after migration. That proves there is no residual host mapping (no fork).

### Owner smoke checks (owed; never marked passed by the executor)

- **DW:** each of the four styles on the Drops row, the compact card and the detail header, for main and off-spec. The proc burst plays once.
- **QC:** the icon glow in each style × always/hover/send on pad and dial, the button glow on pad buttons, and hover in combat.
- **KickCD:** the ready glow in each style for the primary and secondary slots, a knob slider change restarting the glow, and the interruptible-only trigger hiding uninterruptible casts.

## 9. Standard ripple (v2.86.0)

**library-stack-§2, a new row** (after LibDeflate). It is kept short, per the challenger's note on §2's `Lib | When` cells:

`| LibCustomGlow-1.0 | any addon that draws a button, proc, pixel or autocast glow; driven through LibKa0s-Glow-1.0 (library-stack-§7), which resolves it with LibStub(…, true) at call time — absent, no glow |`

The headless-suite claim stays out of the row.

**library-stack-§7, module table:** a new row in `tests/majors.lua` order (after `Item`):

`| LibKa0s-Glow-1.0 | Glow.lua | the stateless LibCustomGlow-1.0 driver: Start(frame, style, knobs, key, frameLevel) and Stop(frame, style, key) map one of the four styles (button, proc, pixel, autocast) and its knob values to LCG's positional arguments, with LCG's two traps handled (pixelLength 0 → nil; a boolean is false only when false). It resolves LibCustomGlow-1.0 at call time and does nothing without it. No defaults, no ranges, no lifecycle: the unchanged-repaint gate, the proc burst and the triggers stay the host's. Ships from LibKa0s v1.75.0 (Glow minor 1); adopters DropWatcher, QuickComms, KickCD |`

**§7 counts paragraph:** "fifteen LibStub majors across thirty-four files" is already stale (the XML has 36 `<Script>` lines at `d9f9454`). Restate the figures by **recount at the v1.75.0 release commit**: `grep -c 'major = "LibKa0s-' tests/majors.lua` and `grep -c '<Script file=' LibKa0s/LibKa0s.xml`, never by increment. Glow contributes +1 major and +1 file. Sim-1.0, and any new Widgets secondary files for SearchBox and TestStrip, land in the same release and must be counted by the same commands. Add a v1.75.0 clause to the running history in the paragraph's style.

**§7 inter-module dependencies:**
- "Fourteen of the fifteen majors floor on Core" and "ten of those fourteen gate on it without calling a single member" become recounted figures. Glow joins the **member-free** list beside `Env`, `Compat`, `Lifecycle`, `Bus`, `Schema`, `Pool`, `Item`, `Media`, `Launcher` and `Options`.
- Add one sentence beside the Bus/AceEvent precedent: "`LibKa0s-Glow-1.0` resolves `LibCustomGlow-1.0` at call time and answers `false` without it, declaring no floor: the payload cannot contain a consumer-vendored lib (library-stack-§6), so there is nothing to floor on, and the §2 row is what lists it."

**§7 fork sentence:** after "Hand-rolling any of these … is forking the toolkit (anti-patterns #47)", add "from v2.86.0 that includes a host START/STOP table over LibCustomGlow-1.0".

The standard changelog line goes in v2.86.0 together with the owner's other v2.86.0 items. No playbook or anti-pattern range changes are needed beyond the #47 mention.

1. LibKa0s: `Glow.lua`, XML, majors.lua, `tests/test_glow.lua`, the DebugLogDiagnostics list, its minor bump and new test, the generated manifest, the API docs, README, releasing.md and CHANGELOG. Green gate.

5. Close #56's driver half as done. Its other candidates are already closed as rejected (the owner's decision 4).

# WowAddonStandards v2.86.0 and dev-copilot 2.4.0: consolidated change set

**Bundle:** `docs/2026-10-22-LIBKA0S_ISSUES_45_58/` (Ka0sAddonsCommonTasks). **Branch in every touched repo:** `feat/2026-10-22-libka0s-issues-45-58`.
**Inputs:** the owner decisions in the task; `analysis.json` (clusters c45 to c58, survey); and the live text of `WowAddonStandards@6bb1bc7` (v2.85.0), `dev-copilot@276ce68` (2.3.5, byte-identical to the installed `~/.claude/plugins/cache/dev-copilot/dev-copilot/2.3.5`) and `LibKa0s@d9f9454` (unreleased v1.75.0, kit 40). Everything was read-only. This document is the design. Nothing has been written to any repo.

---

## 0. Classification, sequencing and assumptions

**Standard bump: minor, v2.85.0 → v2.86.0.** It adds new MUSTs: launcher-§6, the preview-mode marker, the documentation-§1 `gi:` credit, and the closed set of library-drawn icons. It adds one new SHOULD (TestStrip in standalone-windows) and two anti-patterns (#96, #97). The rest are clarifications: automated-tests-§3 crash handling, the library-stack-§7 `__` rule and the hazard-row correction.

**Plugin bump: minor, dev-copilot 2.3.5 → 2.4.0.** `wow-revendor-libka0s` gains behavior: the icon declaration and the prune. Three readers gain the crashed bucket.

**Order the run must keep (hard dependencies):**
1. **The standard's v2.86.0 commits on the branch**, before LibKa0s is tagged:
   - The `__` clause in library-stack-§7 must exist before or with OptionsTabs minor 9. The c45 challenger made this a precondition for the #45 payload removal.
   - LibKa0s release step 7 checks its README standards pointer against `head -1 ../WowAddonStandards/standards/STANDARDS.md`.
2. **LibKa0s v1.75.0 tagged** (kit 41). The figures in §A11 are then recounted at that commit.
3. **dev-copilot 2.4.0 merged, then the owner runs `/plugin update` and `/reload-plugins`.** This must happen before any consumer re-vendor. Per memory (*Use the installed plugin*), the sweep runs only through the installed command. The c55_57 challenger warns that a 2.3.5 sweep leaves every consumer unpruned: green, but in breach of library-stack-§7, *What ships is exactly what is declared*.
4. **Per addon:**
   - `wow-revendor-libka0s` to v1.75.0: declaration, prune, blockers and credits all in one commit.
   - The adoptions.
   - `wow-revendor-standards` to v2.86.0.
5. **GitHub issue actions** (§C), only after the owner's merge go-ahead, with spacing between writes.

**Library layout this document assumes.** It comes from the analyses. The LibKa0s design for this run is authoritative, so correct the figures in §A11 against it before committing:
- `Widgets.lua` minor 12 → 13: `SearchBox` and `TestStrip`, sharing the file-local dropdown `SKIN`.
- New `WidgetsStepPanel.lua` (WidgetsStepPanel minor 1): `StepPanel`.
- `Item.lua` minor 2 → 3: `BonusIDsFromLink`.
- New `Glow.lua` (LibKa0s-Glow-1.0, minor 1).
- New `Sim.lua` (LibKa0s-Sim-1.0, minor 1; it floors on Widgets for StepPanel).
- Comment-only minors: OptionsTabs 9 (the #45 removal), Core 11, DebugLog 20, OptionsIdList 5 (the stale icon comments).
- PerfPanel gets a minor bump only if it is rebuilt on StepPanel.
- Result: **17 majors**. Files: 36 (actual today; the standard's "thirty-four" is already stale) + 3 = **39**.

---

## A. WowAddonStandards v2.86.0: ordered edit list

Write everything in US English and LF. Cite sections as `filename-§N`. `preview-mode` and `standalone-windows` are among the eleven files with no numbered subsections, so add **only unnumbered** headings there. A `### N.` heading would make check-standard's citation check misread them.

### A1. `standards/standards/launcher.md`: new `### 6.` (MUST), plus edits to §2 and §5

**§2, the bullet "Clicking an entry toggles it through the addon's OWN handler".** After "…*Show window* through the window's own toggle (standalone-windows), or the display's `toggle` verb.", insert:

> That same handler is what the addon's Show window key binding presses (launcher-§6): the menu entry, the `toggle` verb and the key are three surfaces onto one handler.

**§2, the bullet "An entry appears exactly when…".** Leave it unchanged ("a dial opened by a keybinding" is not a primary display).

**New section, appended after §5:**

> ### 6. The Show window key binding (MUST)
>
> An addon whose launcher has a **Show window** entry (launcher-§2; its `ADDONS.md` row) **MUST** ship one key binding that toggles that window or display. A player then reaches the thing the addon exists to show without the minimap, a broker display or a slash verb. At v2.86.0 that is six addons:
> - Bank Ledger, Drop Watcher, Loot History, Multi Meters and WhatGroup owe the binding.
> - Quick Comms ships *Toggle Comms Pads*, the reference implementation.
>
> - **One binding, one handler.** The binding **MUST** be a `CLICK` binding in the addon's root `Bindings.xml` (layout-§1). It names a **plain, named, hidden, non-secure** `Button` that a module creates at load and registers with `RegisterForClicks("AnyDown")`, so one press toggles once. Its `OnClick` **MUST** call **the handler the launcher descriptor's `toggleWindow` calls**, which the `toggle` verb and the menu entry already share (launcher-§2). Not allowed:
>   - a second handler or a global function;
>   - Lua in the `<Binding>` element;
>   - a secure template. The window is non-secure (standalone-windows), and a secure button would add combat rules the window does not have.
>
>   ```xml
>   <Bindings>
>     <Binding name="CLICK <Folder>Toggle<Window>:LeftButton" header="<FOLDERUPPER>" category="ADDONS"/>
>   </Bindings>
>   ```
>
>   An addon that already ships bindings, such as Quick Comms' dials, adds this one beside them. It goes under its existing `header`, which only the file's first `<Binding>` carries.
> - **The button's name is permanent.** It is `<Folder>Toggle<Window>` (`QuickCommsTogglePads`). The client stores a player's key against the binding's name, so renaming the button silently unbinds every player's key.
> - **Labels come from the module, through the locale.**
>   - `BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>` is the addon's brand name, `Ka0s <Name>` (launcher-§1).
>   - `BINDING_NAME_CLICK <button>:LeftButton` is a localized label naming the action (`Toggle <window>`).
>
>   Both are assigned in the module that creates the button. The second needs `rawset`, because its name holds a space and a colon.
> - **No default key.** `Bindings.xml` **MUST NOT** carry a `default` attribute. Any key the addon picks collides with somebody's existing binding. The player chooses in the client's Key Bindings → AddOns menu.
> - **A press while stood down refuses exactly as the toggle verb does (MUST).**
>   - It toggles nothing, writes nothing, and prints **exactly one line** through the addon's own printer.
>   - The line is chosen by hold (slash-commands-§7, *Which refusal, by hold*). While the `disabled` hold is taken it is the disabled refusal line. While only the `perf` hold is taken it is `Not available during a performance capture.`, and **never** the disabled line.
>   - A press is a feature, not setup (slash-commands-§7, *The launcher while disabled*). It comes through the addon's one refusal helper:
>     - Where the toggle handler already refuses through that helper, the button just calls it.
>     - Where the handler relies on the dispatcher's gate instead, the button's `OnClick` asks the helper first.
>
>     A third wording is never acceptable.
>   - A silent press is the failure this bullet exists for. The player pressed a key and nothing told them why nothing happened.
> - **Combat.** A press follows the handler's combat contract and adds none. A non-secure window opens and closes in combat (standalone-windows). A display that a secure driver moves defers exactly as its toggle already does (Quick Comms' pads).
> - **Documented.** The README's `## Usage` names the binding and where to set it (Key Bindings → AddOns → `Ka0s <Name>`). `docs/settings-panel.md`'s launcher row lists it beside the *Show window* entry.
> - **Why this is not a library helper (recorded rejection, LibKa0s#58).**
>   - The client reads `Bindings.xml` only from the addon's root, so the file is per addon whatever a library does.
>   - A helper could own about six lines: a named button, its click registration, and two label globals. That is the high-frequency, low-content shape library-stack-§7 keeps inline.
>   - A library writing `BINDING_HEADER_*` on a consumer's behalf would split ownership of a global that an addon with bindings of its own already writes.
>   - **Re-check if** this rollout produces two or more binding buttons that diverge on correctness (a missing or wrong refusal, a double toggle, a secure template, a default key), or if a second binding per addon (Locked, Test mode) is ruled in.
> - **Commencement.** Each owing addon's next release. Missing, mis-shaped or silent bindings are **anti-pattern #96**.

**§5, "Adopting it": append one paragraph:**

> **The Show window key binding (v2.86.0) is a fourth adoption, and it needs no library tag.** Per owing addon: create the button and its labels in the module that owns the window toggle; add the `CLICK` line to a root `Bindings.xml`, creating the file if needed (layout-§1); extend `tests/test_disabled.lua` step 8 (slash-commands-§7); and document it (launcher-§6).

### A2. `standards/standards/layout.md` §1: generalize `Bindings.xml`

- **Tree comment** (lines 12–13). Replace it with:

  `Bindings.xml -- key bindings: owed by every addon with a Show window entry (launcher-§6), else ONLY if the addon ships bindings; client-mandated name and place, beside the TOC; no Lua beyond what the client requires; NOT a TOC line (layout-§1)`

- **The MUST paragraph** (line 101). Replace "a `CLICK` binding on a secure button needs none at all" with:

  > a `CLICK` binding on a named button needs none at all, whether the button is secure (Quick Comms' dial headers) or the plain, hidden button every Show window binding presses (launcher-§6)

  Replace "An addon with no key bindings has no such file." with:

  > An addon with no key bindings has no such file, and since v2.86.0 an addon with a Show window entry always has one (launcher-§6).

- **"Why the root has to hold it"** (line 103). Append:

  > Since v2.86.0 the file is no longer one addon's exception. launcher-§6 makes it owed by every addon whose launcher has a Show window entry, so the root carries it in six repositories, and the MUSTs above are unchanged for all of them.

`toc-file.md:70` ("MUST NOT list `Bindings.xml`") needs no edit.

### A3. `standards/standards/slash-commands.md` §7

- ***Which refusal, by hold*, last bullet.** Change "A feature verb, a button press and any other site" to:

  > A feature verb, a button press, a key binding's press (launcher-§6) and any other site

- ***The launcher while disabled*.** Insert a new bullet after the bullet "A launcher click MUST NOT write SavedVariables…":

  > - **A key press is a feature, and it refuses (MUST).** The Show window binding (launcher-§6) is not setup. A press while the addon is stood down toggles nothing, writes nothing, and prints the one line that *Which refusal, by hold* picks. A grayed menu entry can show its state. A key cannot, so the line is the only answer the player gets, and a silent press is a finding.

- ***The conformance test every addon ships*, step 8.** Rename it **"The launcher and the key binding"** and append:

  > Where the addon ships launcher-§6's binding, invoke its button's `OnClick` (the button the binding names) while disabled. Assert exactly one line matching *The refusal line*, zero SavedVariables writes and zero frame shows. Then write `enabled = true`, take the `perf` hold alone, and invoke it again. Assert exactly one `Not available during a performance capture.` line, no match on *The refusal line*, and no toggle.

### A4. `standards/standards/preview-mode.md`: the marker MUST, and the simulator

**Insert after the "MUST ship a test mode" bullet:**

> - **A test mode MUST say so on the display (v2.86.0).** While test mode is on, every display drawing placeholder data **MUST** carry a visible **text** marker that it is showing test data. The marker:
>   - is readable without hovering;
>   - is localized (localization);
>   - is visible in **every layout in which the placeholder data is visible**, including a hidden header, a compact layout and a collapsed title bar.
>
>   The measured failure: a meter window's `TEST MODE` title text disappeared with its header while the sample bars stayed (Multi Meters, header turned off). The marker's form is the addon's choice: a title badge, inline title text, or a strip. For a standalone window with a filter bar, standalone-windows names the recommended form.
>
>   What is not a marker:
>   - The launcher tooltip's `Test mode: On` and the Master-controls checkbox, because neither is on the display.
>   - Placeholder data that only looks plausible. Placeholder data whose visible text itself names the test (a group popup titled *Test Group*) **is** a marker.
>
>   Under the exception above, where unlocking is the preview, the unlocked display's drag handle (`LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0`'s `DragHandle`, a labeled strip, or the host's equivalent label) is the marker, and nothing more is owed. Missing, hover-only or layout-hidden markers are **anti-pattern #97**.

**Append an unnumbered sub-heading at the end of the file:**

> ### The in-game simulator (MAY)
>
> An addon **MAY** ship an in-game simulator: a session that plays scripted events through its real engine so a player can watch it work without a group, an instance or a real loot event. Drop Watcher's `/dw sim` is the reference, and Loot History and Bank Ledger ship one from v2.86.0.
>
> An addon that ships one:
> - **MUST** build it on **`LibKa0s-Sim-1.0`** (LibKa0s v1.75.0). A private session, seam, timeline or step panel beside the major is anti-pattern #47.
> - **MUST** route every client read the simulation answers through its `NS.Compat` table (compat), because that table is what the seam wraps. The seam must be installed after the compat family loads. A read cached in a local before then answers live data during a session, silently.
> - **MUST** refuse to start:
>   - while the addon is stood down, with the line by hold (slash-commands-§7);
>   - while test mode is on;
>   - in combat, in an instance, or in a group.
>
>   The major computes the last three. The host supplies the first two through its descriptor.
> - **MUST NOT**:
>   - send anything: every outward member (chat, whisper, addon message, trade) is in the host's guarded set;
>   - act on a real player;
>   - write SavedVariables from a simulated event. A session log the host keeps in memory and drops at stop is not SavedVariables.
> - **MUST** leave the addon exactly as it was at stop. Every module the session touched registers its cleanup.
> - **MUST** mark the session while it runs, like test mode (the marker bullet above). The major's step panel on screen satisfies this.
>
> These are the host's contract. The library guarantees only the refusal it computes, and it never advertises the rest as enforced (the LibKa0s#54 record).

### A5. `standards/standards/standalone-windows.md`: a SHOULD naming `W.TestStrip`

**Insert after the "A wide action button keeps its label…" bullet:**

> - **A window with a filter bar marks test mode with the library's strip (SHOULD, v2.86.0).** A standalone window whose body sits under a filter bar **SHOULD** satisfy preview-mode's marker rule with `LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0`'s **`TestStrip`** (Widgets minor 13, LibKa0s v1.75.0). The strip:
>   - spans the window's full width between the filter bar and the body;
>   - carries the catalog's `info` mark and one line saying what test mode shows and what ends it, plus a tooltip;
>   - shifts the body by its own height while it shows, and folds to a compact height when the window is narrow.
>
>   A window with no filter bar keeps whatever marker satisfies preview-mode (a title badge, inline title text), and **MAY** use the strip too. Multi Meters does, because its header, and the marker in it, can be hidden.
>
>   Once an addon is on v1.75.0, a host-built copy of the strip is anti-pattern #47. Drop Watcher is the strip's origin, and Loot History, Bank Ledger and Multi Meters adopt it.

### A6. `standards/standards/anti-patterns.md`: #96 and #97 new, #92 and #95 amended

- **#92**, the sentence "…and over a function literal in a `for ... in` header;": add, after it,

  > and, worse, a **keyed** function literal in a multi-line `for`/`while` header table makes it **raise**, so the run measured nothing and the traceback was read as its footer (a **crashed** run, automated-tests-§3)

  Change "and treat a blind file as complexity not passing" to:

  > and treat a blind file **or a crashed run** as complexity not passing

- **#95**, the sentence beginning "The commonest case is one the host never wrote: the library draws `close`, `copy` and `clear`…": rewrite it to name the closed set from A11:

  > the library draws `close` (every `Core.MakeCloseButton` window), `copy` and `clear` (the debug console's title bar), `info` (an `Options` id list's help mark, and `Widgets.TestStrip`) and `confirm` (`Widgets.StepPanel`'s completed step, so the `Sim` panel too)

  Append the clause:

  > and, upstream, a library release that starts resolving a catalog name outside that closed set from a host's folder (library-stack-§7)

- **New #96:**

  > 96. **A Show window with no key binding, or a binding that is a second feature.** Any of these:
  >     - An addon whose `ADDONS.md` row lists *Show window* and ships no binding for it.
  >     - A binding whose button runs anything but the handler the launcher's `toggleWindow` calls.
  >     - A `<Binding>` element carrying Lua or calling a global function.
  >     - A secure template on a non-secure window's toggle.
  >     - A shipped `default` key.
  >     - A button registered for both click edges, so one press toggles twice.
  >     - A press that toggles, writes or stays silent while the addon is stood down, or that prints the disabled line under the `perf` hold alone.
  >     - A renamed button, which silently unbinds every player's key.
  >
  >     (`launcher-§6`, `layout-§1`, `slash-commands-§7`)

- **New #97:**

  > 97. **A test mode that does not say so.** Any of these:
  >     - Placeholder data drawn with no visible text marker, so sample names read as real ones.
  >     - A marker visible only on hover, or only in the launcher's tooltip or the Master-controls checkbox.
  >     - A marker a layout option hides while the sample data stays visible. Multi Meters with its header turned off is the measured case.
  >     - An unlocalized marker string.
  >     - A simulation session whose displays are unmarked.
  >
  >     (`preview-mode`, `standalone-windows`)

`STANDARDS.md` changes its range to `(#1–#97)`. `check-standard.sh`'s anti-patterns check enforces the 1..N numbering and the index range.

### A7. `standards/standards/documentation.md` §1: icon-set credits

- **Item 12** (line 95). Replace the opening clause "**`## Credits`** — **MAY**, and **only** for genuinely **external** credit…" with:
