blocking: B1. Stale async callbacks and re-entrant Stop are not specified, and the library owns the step machine. (a) `ready()` is only described as 'a second call is ignored'. It has to be bound to the session that issued it. Otherwise a restart, or a stop then start, inside the async build window lets the old `prepare`'s `ready()` mark the new session ready while its world is still unbuilt. DW guards this today with `if Sim.Session() ~= s then return end` (DropWatcher/modules/SimScenario.lua:289). (b) Stop can be re-entered from inside Fire->deliver (the design's own Fire self-stop on stand-down, BL `L:Dispatch` calling Stop('bank'), LH interference, DW auto-stop rows), from inside play, a listener, or an OnStop/OnStopGuarded callback. Because `IsActive()` stays true during `stopping`, a nested Stop re-runs the whole sequence. Fix: Stop answers false once `stopping` is set. Step, Run ticks and RunTo must also capture the session token before play and bail if it changed afterwards (no ranAt/detail stamp, no STEP_LINE, no next tick), as DW's tick does with `if timeline() ~= t then return end` (SimScenario.lua:183). Add tests for each.

B2. RunTo and Run interleave without a rule. Under BL's and LH's gate, RunTo becomes asynchronous: it polls every 0.25 s while the gate is closed. The design keeps `playing` for Run only, so a Run, Step, Pause or second click-ahead during a polling RunTo can double-play or skip steps, and Pause has no defined effect on RunTo. Put RunTo's pending poll in the same `playing` slot, so Run answers `playing`, Pause cancels it and Stop cancels it. Alternatively, refuse RunTo while the gate is closed and print the gate line. Either way, write the rule into the contract and test it.

B3. DeliverForCleanup drops DW's stood-down check. DW's `Sim.DeliverForCleanup` answers 0 when `NS.IsStoodDown()` (DropWatcher/modules/Sim.lua:207-211). Lifecycle records `down` before it calls the standDown callback (LibKa0s/Lifecycle.lua:103), so at a stand-down stop DW never delivers PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED or BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED (SimEvents.lua:511-515) into a torn-down addon. The design's DeliverForCleanup checks only the phase. Through `Stop('standDown')`, called by H6 and by the Fire self-stop, it would deliver cleanup events into a stood-down addon. That changes DW's behaviour and breaks the stand-down invariant. Fix: DeliverForCleanup answers 0 when `isStoodDown()`, which also needs a test.

B4. Host members and the library instance collide. Today DW hangs host members on NS.Sim: `Status` (with DW fields `sends`, `situation`, `members`, read by settings/SimVerbs.lua:117 and diagnostics), `HistoryLog` (History.lua:413,424), `MarkGUID`, `SetRestriction`, `SetLockdown` and `Refusal`. The design never says where these go once NS.Sim is the library instance. If the host sets them on the instance, it shadows `sim:Status()` today, and any field it adds can be shadowed by a future additive Sim minor. Under additive-only-forever that is a silent break. The host contract has to say: (i) the instance is closed and host members live on a host table (for example NS.SimHost); (ii) what NS.Sim and NS.SimSeam are and when each exists. DW's SimWorld and SimEvents call `Sim.SetProvider` at load (SimWorld.lua:505, SimEvents.lua:507), and the sim object has no SetProvider, so hosts must hold the seam separately; (iii) dot-call to colon-call is a mechanical rewrite at every site (about 70 `Sim.X` uses across DW's sim files plus 16 outside them).

B5. Height re-pinning has no Core API, and the design leaves it as 'verify'. `core.MakeResizable` is documented 'Call it once' (LibKa0s/Core.lua:647-648). It sets bounds once through a private `setBounds` (:583-590) and offers no way to update them. Under `widthOnly`, max height equals min height, fixed at call time (:578). Sim's row count changes per scenario and per picker choice in the idle preview, so a resize drag snaps to the stale height. Calling MakeResizable again builds a second grip. Decide now: either (a) StepPanel re-sets bounds itself with a guarded `frame:SetResizeBounds(minW, h, maxW, h)` on each Refresh, a small private duplicate of Core's guard; or (b) Core gains an additive member, which needs Core minor 11 and a new contract. Option (a) is the smaller surface. Then pin the behaviour in test_widgets_step_panel.lua.

B6. W.StepPanel's publicity is decided before the evidence that justifies it. D3 makes the widget public only because Perf becomes its second consumer, yet the PerfPanel rebuild is the LAST commit and is dropped if test_perf_panel.lua needs any edit. If it is dropped, the tag ships a permanent public widget with one in-library consumer, which is the exact scope cut the c53 challenger asked for ('build the panel as a Sim-private file'). Reorder: do the PerfPanel-on-StepPanel spike right after WidgetsStepPanel.lua, before any Sim file. If it fails, move the widget into Sim as a library-private file before anything is tagged.

B7. 'Tag once' freezes surface that only the not-yet-built hosts use. `gate`, `stepDelay` as a function, `pure` used as 'client read never simulated' (BL), `hook:<name>` pseudo-events (LH), `OnStopGuarded` with no Reconcile (BL) and `refusal` with per-scenario prerequisites (LH) have no consumer at tag time. DW uses none of `gate`, function `stepDelay` or pseudo-events, so bar 1 ('same semantics') is unproven for them. If a gap turns up in LH or BL after the tag, it needs a v1.76 additive minor, which contradicts owner decision (1). Either hold the v1.75.0 tag until thin LH and BL sim skeletons (seam, deliver, one scenario, gate, stop phases) are green against the branch payload, or ask the owner to accept a later additive minor up front.

B8. The DW contract proof contradicts itself. §12 step 4 says DW 'must pass unchanged integration suites'. §10 allows 'assertion edits confined to moved and deleted tests'. Neither is achievable as written: test_sim_e2e.lua calls `NS.SimScenario.Start/Run/Status/STEP_DELAY`, `NS.Sim.Stop`, `NS.Sim.Live` and `NS.Sim.SeamKeys` 23 times (for example :126, :287-303, :332-341, :356-413). Library-emitted lines also differ from DW's today: Restart uses Stop('restart') where DW uses Stop('stop') (SimScenario.lua:338), an unknown scenario prints UNKNOWN_SCENARIO plus the names where DW prints 'Unknown scenario.', and `help` is new. Restate the proof: call sites are rewritten mechanically, and every observable assertion (printed lines through host overrides, store and feed state, sends counts) stays byte-identical. List each library-induced line change as an accepted delta.

TEST_STRIP.RESERVE contradicts the design's own contract and fails the minimal-surface bar. Section 2.3 says placement and body shift are host layout. DropWatcher keeps its own K.BANNER_H = 22 anyway (section 6.1), so RESERVE's only real readers are three hosts that would be adopting DropWatcher's spacing. lib.TEST_STRIP is also a process-wide mutable table. The design's '99' test shows that a host write cannot move the strip, but the same write moves every other addon's body shift, because hosts read RESERVE live. Publish HEIGHT only, the one figure the widget itself owns (the DRAG_HANDLE precedent covers this), and let each host write its own gap. If the owner wants RESERVE regardless, record in the API doc that it encodes a 2 px gap convention and is not a placement contract.

Published region fields go beyond any consumer's need. The design makes strip.fill, strip.icon and strip.text public contract, and under section 7 'non-__ is contract' they stay forever. Only strip.text has a consumer: DropWatcher's layoutStrip needs SetText and SetWordWrap, CC.BannerH measures it, and MultiMeters, LootHistory and BankLedger set text. fill and icon are read only by tests and by DropWatcher's b.art to b.icon rename, which exists only because the field was published. That is negligible and event-driven, but it is a behaviour difference from today's early return, and the design's 'which is today's outcome' covers only the state, not the work. Record it in divergence 13, or keep a cheap host-side early-out (`self._glowUnavailable`).

blocking: A11.1 (the `__` clause) is factually wrong for LibKa0s and unsafe as a rule. Several `__` members are documented contract that consumers already call. `lib.__PatchLSM30Border` is documented at docs/api/Options/version-29.2.34.2.4.8.1.7.4.2.1-docs.md:1317 and called at AbsorbTracker/settings/OptionsSetup.lua:370. `lib.__IsCombatLocked` (docs :914 and :1371) is called at MultiMeters/settings/OptionsSetup.lua:670. `optlib.__AttachCompose` is called at MultiMeters/settings/Schema_Compose.lua:479. `O.__panels` is a documented host test seam (docs :1476) used at BankLedger/settings/Panel.lua:644. `lib.__PreloadFonts` and `lib.__railInset` are documented members too. A blanket rule that '`__` is not contract, MAY be removed once nothing in the payload, suites, majors.lua or testkit reaches it' leaves out the roster consumers. Under LibStub's newest-copy-wins, removing any of these would break AbsorbTracker or MultiMeters at runtime, and 'a consumer MUST NOT call a `__` member' would make two addons non-compliant on the day it lands. Fix: make the clause narrow. It covers only a `__` member whose API document classes it as an internal or attach/test seam AND that has zero roster-consumer references (code, tests and stubs, census across all 14 addons at the removal tag). Members that are documented and consumer-called are contract until a major bump. Drop the consumer MUST NOT, or grandfather the named members.

A11.6, A6 (#95), A17 and A19 put `info` (TestStrip) and `confirm` (StepPanel/Sim) in the closed library-drawn set, which contradicts how Widgets works. LibKa0s/Widgets.lua:12-17 says Widgets cannot depend on Media because a vendored copy cannot know its host folder, so all art arrives as resolved-path parameters. The c48 analysis confirms TestStrip's info mark must be host-passed, and the c53 StepPanel contract has `check = texture path or nil`, which the host supplies (DW passes `NS.Icon('confirm')`). These are host-drawn names, already caught by the host-seam derivation, and not library-resolved ones. The paragraph 'if Perf's panel draws confirm, every Perf host owes confirm, so its rebuild keeps its color dots' rests on the same false premise: Perf just passes no `check`. The design also breaks its own rule ('new chrome takes art from the host'). Fix: the set stays `close, copy, clear, info` (info = the OptionsIdList default only). Sim takes its check path from the host descriptor. Remove the TestStrip/Sim declaration clauses from A11.6, #95, A17, A19 and the B1 3i(c) text.
